children: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a combined ₹1.51 crore over alleged disclosure and compliance lapses, including a related-party transaction (RPT) disclosure issue and audit reports signed by firms without valid peer-review certificates.

Adani Enterprises paid ₹76.05 lakh, Adani Green Energy ₹45.50 lakh, while Adani Total Gas, AWL Agri Business and Adani Energy Solutions paid ₹9.75 lakh each. The five companies settled the proceedings without admitting or denying the findings of fact and conclusions of law.

The proceedings stemmed from a SEBI examination into allegations relating to RPT disclosures and corporate governance issues highlighted in the January 2023 Hindenburg Research report. The examination covered seven Adani group companies, including the five that have now settled the matter.

For AEL, SEBI’s show-cause notice alleged that RPTs between Adani Estates, a subsidiary of AEL, and Vakoder Investment, a related party, were not disclosed in the company’s FY13 annual report as required under the applicable accounting standard.

The notice also alleged that AEL’s audit report for FY15 and limited review report for the June 2015 quarter were signed by Dharmesh Parikh & Co LLP without a valid Peer Review Certificate. Further, its limited review reports for the June and September 2017 and December 2021 quarters were allegedly signed by Shah Dhandharia & Co LLP without a valid certificate.

For Adani Total Gas and AWL Agri Business, SEBI cited their December 2021 limited review reports, which were allegedly signed by Shah Dhandharia without a valid Peer Review Certificate. For Adani Green, the alleged lapse related to its FY19 audit report and limited review reports for September 2018, December 2018 and June 2019, signed by Dharmesh Parikh. The Adani Energy Solutions proceedings related to its June 2015 limited review report.

The companies proposed settlement in the pending adjudication proceedings in 2024. SEBI’s High Powered Advisory Committee recommended the revised terms in June 2026, which were accepted by the Whole-time Members in August. The companies remitted the amounts in September, after which SEBI disposed of the proceedings.

The settlement comes a year after SEBI dismissed separate allegations concerning certain transactions involving Adani group entities, while other proceedings arising from the Hindenburg-related examination have been dealt with separately.

title: SEBI settles proceedings against five Adani firms for ₹1.51 crore
